pr_title: fix(test runner): align with typescript behaviour for resolving `index.js` and `package.json` through path mapping
pr_body:
Supercedes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/31915, closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/31811.

When TypeScript resolves a specifier via path mapping, it does not interpret `package.json`. If path mapping resolves to a directory, it only looks at the `index.js` file in that directory if it's in CommonJS mode.

We need to mirror this in our `esmLoader.ts`.

issue_context.title: [Regression]: ESM Directory Import is not working anymore with Playwright's ESM Loader activated
issue_context.body:
### Last Good Version

1.42

### First Bad Version

1.43

### Steps to reproduce

Repo + Reproduction steps are in the repository: https://github.com/schickling-test/2024-playwright-esm-repro



### Expected behavior

Works

### Actual behavior

Error: Directory import '/Users/maxschmitt/Developer/tmp/2024-playwright-esm-repro/packages/@acme/lib' is not supported resolving ES modules imported from /Users/maxschmitt/Developer/tmp/2024-playwright-esm-repro/packages/@acme/tests/src/hello.test.ts

### Additional context

We run into this if for the directory import: https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/blob/d23ea26947d6b9644ddc92702796d7682d206fc6/packages/playwright/src/transform/esmLoader.ts#L30

and then pass the directory as a `file://` URL to the defaultResolver which breaks.

I throws here: https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/e192a32c27f223e7a3dcb43134fd891dd8ded760/lib/internal/modules/esm/resolve.js#L254

Workaround, add a check like `!require('fs').statSync(resolved).isDirectory()`.

### Environment

```shell
N/A
```
comments:
I have this error when I run npx playwright test:

**Error: Directory import 'C:\Users\mirnesz\Desktop\Projekti\frontend-dev\node_modules\@mui\material\Stack' is not supported resolving ES modules imported from C:\Users\mirnesz\Desktop\Projekti\frontend-dev\src\components\custom-datagrid\enhanced-datagrid-container.tsx
Did you mean to import "@mui/material/node/Stack/index.js"?**


My playwright version is: **"@playwright/test": "^1.45.3"**

TypeScript explicitly discourages using `paths` together with monorepo imports: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html#paths-should-not-point-to-monorepo-packages-or-node_modules-packages

In the case of the repro, it would work perfectly fine without the `paths` setting in TS Config.

Having said that, we'd still like to be compliant with TypeScript's dependency resolution here. I'll put up a fix shortly.

review_comments:
It seems like TypeScript:
- does not honor `exports` field from `package.json` after the type mapping;
- does honor the default `index.js` and `main` field from `package.json` after the type mapping as explained here: https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/modules/reference.html#directory-modules-index-file-resolution. Note that both `index.js` and `main` are ignored for ESM, as explained here: https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v20.x/docs/api/modules.html#folders-as-modules.

The docs above match my manual testing as well. I think we should follow TS and implement the same logic.

I've added a test to ensure we follow your first observation in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32078/commits/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa.

For the second one, isn't that exactly the behaviour we have right now? If there's a `package.json` file, then we let Node.js deal with resolving to either `index.js` or `main`, depending on the ESM mode.

- For the `exports` field, it looks like the code will defer to Node.js (when not in ESM), and Node will honor the `exports`. Is that not the case?
- For the `main` field, TypeScript also checks various extensions (e.g. `ts`) after following it, and we currently do not, because we leave it to Node.js. That's a minor thing, but it would be ideal to mirror TypeScript there as well.
- Updating comments to explain these things would be great as well!

1. I believe the test https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa/tests/playwright-test/resolver.spec.ts#L609-L644 asserts just that behaviour. Maybe i'm looking at it wrong though.
2. The `.ts` extension is covered by https://github.com/Skn0tt/playwright/blob/9a80386c7d057027499609aa4d648549482474fa/tests/playwright-test/resolver.spec.ts#L572-L607. What other extensions should we cover?

Both of these are about the path mapping case. Are you referring to the case where there's no path mapping?

In https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/pull/32078/commits/62ff3fd736429eb9f3e4038694e4d192944489f8, i've added a test to ensure that `main` is ignored in ESM mode, and updated the comments.
Yep, the tests look like they cover all the cases. I guess for the item 1, Node.js does not look at `exports` either, which works for us. Thank you for following through!
